facts.fact: “有什么区别”笑话常用斯普纳互换首辅音，并故意说半句让听者自己补包袱
facts.anchor: Many involve spoonerisms, swapping the first consonants of the main words, and often trail off to leave the listener to work out the punchline themselves.

facts.fact: 勇敢士兵冲进敌阵——原应说 darts into the fray（fray／foe 首辅音互换），句子在关键处断掉
facts.anchor: A brave soldier darts into the foe …

facts.fact: 英格兰足球队与茶包的区别：茶包在杯子里待得更久
facts.anchor: What’s the difference between the England football team and a teabag? / The teabag stays in the cup longer.

facts.fact: 政府与黑手党的区别：黑手党是有组织的
facts.anchor: What’s the difference between the government and the Mafia? / The Mafia is organized.

facts.fact: 鱼和自行车的区别：两个都会游泳——除了自行车（故意自相矛盾的反笑话）
facts.anchor: What’s the difference between a fish and a bicycle? / They can both swim, except for the bicycle.

facts.fact: 这类“笨族群”笑话在英国以爱尔兰人为靶子，在美国以波兰人为靶子
facts.anchor: The Irish were historically the target of these when told in the UK, while American versions targeted the Polish.

facts.fact: 从效率看用“一个白痴”更好，因为不必假定听者与你共享偏见
facts.anchor: From an efficiency perspective, ‘An idiot’ works better as it doesn’t rely on the person you’re telling the joke to sharing your bigotry.

facts.fact: 换灯泡笑话常用于圈内梗，依赖行业或爱好特有的刻板印象
facts.anchor: Lightbulb jokes are often used in very in-jokey ways, using extremely industry- or hobby-specific stereotypes

facts.fact: 书名＋作者谐音：Rusty Bedsprings by I. P. Knightley（I pee nightly）、Amelia Rating（ameliorating）、Oliver Sudden（all of a sudden）
facts.anchor: Rusty Bedsprings by I. P. Knightley; Attempting to Improve Matters by Amelia Rating; Out of the Blue by Oliver Sudden.

facts.fact: 一旦开始这样想，名字和词很快失去意义，脑子会变成一团糊
facts.anchor: once you start thinking in this way, names and words swiftly lose all meaning and your brain becomes entirely mush
